question:
An astronomical telescope is used in normal adjustment (final image at infinity). The objective is a circular aperture of diameter $D=4.0\,\text{cm}$.

Two distant stars have an angular separation $\Delta\theta=2.36\times10^{-5}\,\text{rad}$ in object space.

Assume the telescope is diffraction-limited by the objective and uses the Rayleigh criterion. Also, treat the light as photons with energy $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

Find the minimum photon energy $E_{\min}$ (in eV) such that the telescope can just resolve the two stars. (Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.)
